title: Roads Without Sidewalks: Pedestrians Walk on the LEFT Shoulder Facing Oncoming Traffic

no_head_on_same_lane.note: Only one vehicle visible on the road; no two vehicles facing each other in same lane.

no_rhd_cabin.note: No vehicle interior or steering wheel visible; only rear exterior of SUV on right.

single_bulb_signal.note: No traffic signal present in rural road scene.

us_right_hand_traffic.note: Car travels on right side of dashed yellow centerline with white edge line on right; correct US right-hand layout.

zero_text.note: License plate is blank white rectangle, diamond warning sign is blank yellow; no letters, numbers or words visible.

scene_match.note: Rural two-lane road with no sidewalks and vest-wearing walker on far-left shoulder matches, but walker faces toward foreground while the adjacent left lane traffic would come toward foreground, so she is not facing oncoming traffic and no oncoming front-facing car is shown.

result.summary: Walker is placed on left shoulder but faces the wrong way, walking with adjacent traffic rather than facing oncoming traffic, teaching the opposite of the rule.

teaching_correct.note: Left-shoulder walker faces toward camera/foreground while left-lane oncoming traffic would approach from behind her toward foreground; she walks with her back to oncoming traffic instead of facing it, teaching the unsafe direction.

result.what_i_see: A woman in a yellow reflective vest walks on the grassy far-left shoulder facing the camera in the foreground, while a black SUV in the right lane drives away from the camera into the distance on a sunny rural two-lane road.
